killed.title: 0.80 bright-block fraction gate counts star pixels, forcing the star rolloff that kills star color and prominence
why: The cited lines exist (quality-gates.mjs:613-615 defaults 50/0.95/3; tools.mjs:2487-2498 0.80 fraction pass vs burn.max_bright_block_pct; stale docstring :596-601 and prompt :677 saying 100x100/0.93), but the central claim that stars trip the 0.80 fraction gate and thereby force star rolloff is not supported. (1) PSF arithmetic: for a Gaussian star, pixels above 0.80 = pi*2*sigma^2*ln(peak/0.80); FWHM 11 px at peak 1.0 gives ~31 px (1.2% of a 50x50 block), FWHM 8 ~16 px, FWHM 6 ~9 px, all below the 3% block threshold (~75 px / 9 of 289 samples). The claimed 100-300 px requires a saturated flat-top plateau of radius 6-10 px, which the pipeline's linear-star/no-erosion rules are built to avoid. (2) A tripped block does not fail the gate; the gate needs >1-2% of ALL blocks (88-176 of 8814 on NGC7635, ~243-485 of ~24k on 60 MP), i.e. hundreds of plateau stars. (3) git show 0aeb967 and 8105a12 confirm the 0.80 pass was a warning from inception and only became a fraction gate after NGC7635 3294686f; it was never zero-tolerance. The star rolloffs in the lessons were driven by the 0.95 hard gate after screen blend: project_ngc7635_3294686f_lessons.md:23 states 'rolloff at 0.65 leaves max 0.811, which causes burns after screen blend onto 0.88 base' (screen(0.81,0.88)=0.977>0.95). Later runs passed the fraction gate with star max 0.811 (6d0b2048) and 0.895 (bc93d9d1), so 'repeatedly use rolloff 0.50' is overstated (only 3294686f and ac00d0cc did). feedback_soft_rolloff_stars.md's 'zero blocks above 0.80' is a memory inaccuracy, not code. (4) The one documented fraction-gate failure (bc93d9d1 lesson :26-27) was the nebula shell pushed above 0.80 by R/Y boosts, exactly the extended-structure case the gate targets; star color loss there came from the agent applying a global post-blend rolloff instead of a masked one. (5) The proposal references brief._starLayerId, which does not exist (grep finds only brief._starIntegrity[viewId]), and a d=12 probe at 0.68 would still classify any plateau star of radius >12 px as extended, so it would not exclude the stars it targets. No run traces in ~/.pixinsight-mcp/runs contain a TOO MANY BRIGHT REGIONS failure either. What remains real is cosmetic/P2: the docstring, prompt and the standalone scan_burnt_regions tool description (tools.mjs:3331, says 32x32 / 0.98 / 5% / 1% limit) are all inconsistent with the actual 50/0.95/3 scan, and the standalone tool never runs the 0.80 fraction pass, so the agent cannot preview this gate before finish.

The causal chain "0.80 fraction gate -> forced star rolloff -> dead star color" does not hold against the code and the surviving run data, so the change would not measurably move the user's goal (brighter, more colorful stars).

1. The 0.80 pass is NOT zero-tolerance and is not tripped by stars in practice. tools.mjs:2487-2498 fails only when the block fraction exceeds burn.max_bright_block_pct (1-8%). The user-approved NGC7023 best-of-both image (run efe2138e, finish seq 181, final max=0.9435, rich Cepheus star field, stars blended) finished with "BRIGHT REGIONS: 26 block(s) (0.3%)" vs a 1.0% limit — a 3x margin even on the strictest profile. A bright star can mark at most 1-4 blocks (with every-3rd-pixel sampling a block needs ~80 px > 0.80), so reaching 1% (~90 blocks) needs dozens of saturated stars. The per-profile headroom was designed precisely so "a FEW bright blocks around a core = OK" (prompt :186).

2. The rolloff that kills star color is mandated elsewhere, independent of this gate: (a) giga-orchestrator.mjs:568-575 "Rolloff knee: 0.65 (standard)" / "Soft rolloff (always)" and processing-profiles.json:92 rolloff_knee 0.65; (b) check_star_layer_integrity FAIL at max >= 0.98 (tools.mjs:3444) refuses star_protected_blend until a rolloff is applied (:1180-1182); (c) the unchanged 0.95 zero-tolerance post-blend scan — the NGC7635 lessons the reviewer cites (3294686f: "rolloff at 0.65 leaves max 0.811, which causes burns after screen blend onto 0.88 base"; 6d0b2048: "strength 0.95 burned at 2-3 blocks") are 0.95 clipping events (screen(0.81, 0.88) ~ 0.98), not fraction-gate failures. The one real fraction-gate-driven rolloff (bc93d9d1 "R/Y boosts push entire shell above 0.80", 3.9% after soft clamp) was extended nebula shell — exactly what the gate exists for. feedback_soft_rolloff_stars.md's "zero blocks above 0.80" wording predates the fraction limit (commit 4722e40, 2026-04-07) and no longer describes the code.

3. The reviewer's own calibration target is self-defeating: raising the star knee to 0.80 pushes star max to ~0.9+; screened onto a 0.85-0.93 base that clips past 0.95 and fails the 0.95 pass the proposal keeps unchanged — so M27/NGC7023 would not pass "with the knee raised to 0.80" regardless of the 0.80 change.

4. The star-layer skip variant carries a real risk on the user's reference case: on NGC7023 the burn/flat-core problem sits in the halo of the illuminating star HD 200775, which lives in the SXT star layer; skipping pixels where the star layer > 0.05 blinds gate 3b exactly there (gate 3c partly covers it, but the user's calibrate-against-known-good rule argues against narrowing a gate on the reference failure zone).

What survives is documentation hygiene, not a P1: three inconsistent descriptions of the same scanner (quality-gates.mjs:596-610 says 100x100/0.93; the scan_burnt_regions tool description tools.mjs:3332 says 32x32/0.98/5%/1% limit; prompt :677 says 0.93; the code is 50/0.95/3%). Severity P2. The actual lever for the user's open "stars MORE prominent" item is the mandatory 0.65 knee + the 0.98/0.95 clip chain, which this proposal does not touch.
